analysis.title: "War Of Attrition": Barclays Reveals The Scariest Chart For The AI Buildout
key_insights: Barclays credit strategists Dominique Toublan and Jonathan Ortega say the midterms brought a blue wave to the grid. AI pushback is bipartisan but local, making the buildout pricier rather than stalling it. The AI race shifts from a prisoner's dilemma to a war of attrition in which scarce power favors the biggest balance sheets.

Barclays says the depth of the Democratic wave was not fully priced and expects some sector spreads to adjust. Texas and Georgia alone account for roughly one-third of AI data center spending, and Democrats flipped or held governorships or legislatures in Texas, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Wisconsin and Michigan.

Of the roughly 300GW of high-probability data center pipeline reported by utilities, about 80% will sit in states with a Democratic governor in 2027, up from under 30% in 2026. The red-state share went from 214GW to 60GW. Texas alone accounts for 105GW, more than the next four states combined.

Texas, Georgia and Ohio flipped from Republican to Democratic governors. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on an immediate data center moratorium. Georgia governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms proposed a temporary pause and the Public Service Commission flipped to a 3-2 Democratic majority. Ohio governor-elect Amy Acton supported a conditional moratorium. Barclays expects further delays for a portion of Texas projects, with the path clearer in 1H 27.

Barclays expects the buildout to become pricier and marginally slower rather than stop, because projects can relocate and federal efforts to speed grid connections continue. Data centers that already have power or are close to it gain a scarcity advantage.

Barclays expects hyperscaler spreads to be largely unaffected. Pressure should concentrate in neoclouds and pipeline data center developers. Assets that already have power should outperform. Companies dependent on capex (power equipment, construction, chip supply chain) face a slower path.

Barclays' AI ecosystem trades roughly 44bps wide of the IG index, versus about 10bps tight a year ago. Excluding hyperscalers the gap is over 20bps. Dispersion between the best and worst AI names has expanded sharply. On Barclays' z-score screen, Intel, Marvell, Oracle, Broadcom and the hyperscalers are in the cheapened-on-both-horizons quadrant.

Barclays' tech credit team says data center permitting risk was viewed as more bark than bite until this week. Of 27 data center bonds across IG and HY, two are fully operational (QTS and Applied Digital), nine are partially complete or due online soon, and four have date-certain rent (RDMICH, RPLDCI, TXEDCI, SECMOS). The market will need to differentiate among bonds by permitting status.

In ZeroHedge's TRACE data, project bonds Barclays flags as operational or nearly so widened about 71bps on average since September 28, versus roughly 105bps for the rest of the project-bond universe and 250-440bps for CoreWeave unsecured paper. The day after the election, Texas-sited project bonds fell an average 0.2 points while project bonds elsewhere rose about 0.4 points. This is one day of prints and a small sample.

All four of CoreWeave's unsecured notes trade between 78.5 and 83 cents, yielding about 15.5%, down 7-10 points since late September. The AI junk bond market was described as bidless on the morning of the article.

On semis, Barclays expects AVGO and NVDA to outperform near term because slower builds slow chip financing, which matters more for credit. Barclays calls it hardly an all-clear for chip financing and questions how sustainable a semis rally would be. Roughly $21B of bonds are being lined up for Broadcom's chip-financing deal, the $63B Anthropic SPV.

Barclays sees negative ramifications for the broader supply chain if hyperscaler capex growth disappoints. It still expects capex to move considerably higher in 2027/28 but says the range of outcomes is wider. Servers and networking (HPE, Dell, Cisco) and semis not tied to chip financing (Intel, Qualcomm, Micron) are in the firing line.

Barclays sees scope for delays to positive catalysts at IPPs (Constellation, Vistra, NRG) but no credit downside risk at this juncture. ERCOT on-peak power is in the low $40s/MWh versus about $90 for PJM West. Vistra has 20.4GW in ERCOT and is the most exposed. Talen is almost entirely PJM. Regulated utilities with exposure to flipped states, such as Southern Co in Georgia, face greater scrutiny on affordability and capex, while T&D utilities are relatively less exposed.

Barclays thematic strategist William Thompson says data centers combine visible infrastructure costs with fewer visible local benefits and have become a physical proxy for anti-AI sentiment, so addressing water and power bills alone may not resolve opposition. Bring-your-own-power models can accelerate deployment and reduce cost-shifting concerns.

Goldman's trading desk called buying hyperscalers versus selling semis the standout theme. The spread between its hyperscaler basket and the SOX was about 5% overnight. Over the past month semis are down 22% versus hyperscalers down 4%.

Goldman estimates state-level moratoria could freeze about 45% of planned US data center capacity. Goldman's Credit MarketStrats team says the widening makes valuations more attractive and would add risk, while noting HY leverage is at its highest since 2021 and expecting dispersion to pick up into next year. BofA's Hartnett has moved from short hyperscaler bonds to telling clients to buy them.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers can outlast the cost increases and consolidation favors the largest balance sheets. Goldman Credit MarketStrats says the widening has made valuations more attractive and would add risk. Hartnett now says buy hyperscaler bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: Barclays says the bar for AI has gone up. Neoclouds and pipeline developers borrowed at 9-12% and face delayed power and permits. HY leverage is at its highest since 2021, and a war of attrition among tenants and developers could reach the hyperscalers that guarantee and backstop them.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas permitting clarity expected in 1H 27, and a hyperscaler capex growth disappointment in 2027/28 would test the view.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays expects AVGO and NVDA to outperform near term as slower builds slow chip financing, and Goldman's desk favors buying hyperscalers versus selling semis.
tension_points.bear_case: Barclays questions how sustainable any semis rally would be, since chip financing deals are still pending syndication in 2027 and capex range of outcomes is wider.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler capex growth disappointing in 2027/28 would undercut the supplier chain.
